Explain the geometric meaning of a vector dot product, including orthogonal vectors and negative projection.

props.label: Signed projection of a onto b

blocks.text: The dot product measures how much one vector points along another. For nonzero b, drop a perpendicular from the tip of a to the line through b. The signed distance from the common starting point to where it lands is the scalar projection of a onto b. Multiply that distance by the length of b: a · b = ‖a‖ ‖b‖ cos θ, where θ is the angle between the vectors.

If the projection lands in the direction b points, the dot product is positive. If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), it lands at the starting point, so the dot product is zero. If it lands on the opposite side, the projection and dot product are negative. A dot product with the zero vector is also zero, even though the angle is undefined.
